files.description: What we are building and for whom. Section 6.2 is the fidelity contract every lesson must satisfy; section 9 is the numbered requirement list (P0-n, P1-n, P2-n) that code and docs cite. Judge changes against these; flag code that satisfies a requirement differently from its acceptance criterion.

Where every word in a lesson comes from: the pinned canon and its loader rules (section 2), the lesson sequence and per-learner position rule (section 3), the pack manifest, ingestion contract, confidence grading, retrieval rules, and composition trace (section 4), composition rules, validation rows, and the banned-word tiers (section 5), fixed texts and the placeholder legend (section 7), the audit log (section 8). Use it to check that code implements the mechanism as defined.

Architecture, protocols, and auth for every edge (section 4), record shapes and mutability rules (section 6), ingestion and delivery sequences (sections 7 and 8), the links service and token format (section 9), commands (section 10), the test plan (section 12), deployment and IAM (section 13), the decision log (section 14), and Appendix B listing hardening that is deliberately deferred. Do not suggest building anything from Appendix B in v1.0.
The phased plan. Use it to judge whether a change belongs to the phase in progress or is scope creep from a later phase.

Tracing helpers carried from v0 with their tests: module-local provider, export gating precedence, structlog processor. Include when reviewing any module so span and logging conventions are checked against the real implementation.
The fake implementations of the store, channel, and model-client seams that unit tests must use. Include when reviewing tests so new tests use the fakes rather than patching SDK internals.
